sentences.text: The name Hypselorhachis means wonderful high spine, combining Latin and Greek roots.
The genus is known from a single vertebra found in the Middle Triassic Manda Beds of Tanzania.
The type species H. mirabilis was mentioned but never fully described by Alan J. Charig.
The authority for both the genus and the species is Butler et al., 2009.
This single known vertebra is slender, measuring only about 20 mm in transverse thickness, though it remains largely intact despite some chipping.
Based on the size of the vertebra, Hypselorhachis was likely at least 3 meters long, possibly reaching 4 or 5 meters.
If Hypselorhachis possessed a full sail, it would have been tough because it was composed mostly of transversely compressed bone with little space between the elements.
The solid and compact neural arch with a thin neural canal suggests the spinal cord was well protected.
In 1988, Hypselorhachis was assigned to the family Ctenosauriscidae, a group of sail-backed archosaurs.
Hypselorhachis is classified within the unranked order Paracrocodylomorpha and the superfamily Poposauroidea.
Hypselorhachis is classified as a reptile.
Hypselorhachis lived during the Middle Triassic period.
The fossil was found in the Lifua Member of the Manda Beds, which dates to the Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic.
Due to the scarcity of fossil material, the current phylogenetic classification of Hypselorhachis remains tentative.
